summary: This RFC adds NFSv4.2 extensions to improve Weak Cache Consistency for the Flexible File Layout in parallel NFS. They make sure partial writes done under a pNFS layout stay coherent and are tracked correctly, addressing concurrency and data integrity problems when several clients write to the same file.

eli5.summary: When many people edit the same notebook, you need to know who wrote which part. This helps a shared file system keep partial changes straight and consistent.

questions: what is weak cache consistency in nfs
how does pnfs update the metadata server
subtitle: A new NFSv4.2 operation lets clients report data-server file attributes to the metadata server in pNFS.

tldr.problem: In the pNFS flexible file layout, data servers have no way to tell the metadata server when a file's data changes, so the metadata server must poll them with costly NFSv3 GETATTR calls.
tldr.mechanism: A new optional NFSv4.2 operation, LAYOUT_WCC (operation 77), lets the client forward the attributes it already received from the data servers (NFSv3 weak cache consistency data) to the metadata server.
tldr.outcome: The metadata server MAY avoid many GETATTR calls to data servers. The operation is OPTIONAL, and the data is only a weak model the server may ignore.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: OPTIONAL for NFSv4.2 and the flexible file layout

today: RFC 9766 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2025, and the unit metadata shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it. It builds on RFC 8435 and RFC 9754.

sections.title: The Missing Update Channel
sections.content:
In the Parallel NFS (pNFS) flexible file layout, there is no mechanism for the data servers to update the metadata server when the data portion of a file changes. The metadata server needs that knowledge to update the metadata portion of the file.

A client using NFSv3 with a data server can use Weak Cache Consistency (WCC) to learn attribute changes. This document introduces a new operation, LAYOUT_WCC, which lets the client periodically report the attributes of the data files to the metadata server.

Following the process in RFC 8178, the changes are an extension of NFSv4.2 (RFC 7862), built on the XDR generated from RFC 7863.
sections.eli5: Right now the data helpers cannot tell the librarian when pages change. This RFC adds a way to pass the news along.

sections.title: Weak Cache Consistency and the Cost of Polling
sections.content:
With the flexible file layout, a client is limited to the NFSv3 operations READ, WRITE and COMMIT on the filehandles in the layout, which act on file data. The metadata server uses NFSv3 CREATE, GETATTR and SETATTR on the data files. GETATTR mainly gives it mtime, ctime and atime, from which it can work out the time_modify, time_metadata and time_access values to give clients in an NFSv4.2 GETATTR response.

The metadata server may issue an NFSv3 GETATTR to the data server whenever a client asks for attributes. Beyond the cost of each call, the data server can be overwhelmed by a large volume of them. NFSv3 handled this by returning post-operation attributes with READ and WRITE (WCC data). NFSv4 dropped that, but pNFS brings the same problem back.

The client can already use NFSv3 WCC to proxy times (RFC 9754), but the data is coarse. With client-side mirroring the client must aggregate N mirrored files into one report, and it can only send it when it returns the delegation.
sections.eli5: Asking the shelf-keeper about every book each time is slow and wears them out. Books handed back with a little note about what changed save the trip.

sections.title: The LAYOUT_WCC Operation
sections.content:
LAYOUT_WCC is operation 77. Its arguments are a stateid (lowa_stateid), a layout type (lowa_type) and an opaque body (lowa_body). The result is only a status, lowr_status. The current filehandle and the stateid identify the layout, and the layout type says how to interpret the body.

The body holds the data file attributes. The client maps NFSv3 post-operation attributes to the NFSv4 fattr4 form. The client may ignore the attributes, and the server may ignore any it receives; the server can use them to avoid querying the data server. Because they are optional and the client has no recourse, the result does not return a bitmap of accepted attributes.

The metadata server MAY avoid costly NFSv3 GETATTR calls. Since this is a weak model, it MAY still make them to strengthen it.
sections.eli5: The helper hands the librarian a note listing what changed. The librarian can trust it, or still go check if they want to be sure.

sections.title: When to Send It and What to Include
sections.content:
The metadata server can only detect data file modifications by probing with GETATTR and comparing mtime across calls; atime shows reads. A client can send LAYOUT_WCC at any time, but is likely to do so when:

  • it sends a GETATTR for size, space_used, change, time_access, time_metadata or time_modify;
  • it reports an NFS4ERR_ACCESS error through LAYOUTRETURN or LAYOUTERROR, since it may already hold the NFSv3 uid and gid from the failing operation;
  • it sends a SETATTR to refresh the proxied times.

The attributes from WRITE, READ and COMMIT are a subset of NFSv4 attributes. LAYOUT_WCC MUST provide all of the mapped attributes shown in the table below. The uid and gid are stringified into owner and owner_group, so the metadata server can compare them with expected values and repair permissions or fix its cache.
sections.eli5: The helper sends the note when someone asks about sizes or times, when a door refused a visitor, or when it refreshes its clocks.

sections.title: The Flexible File Layout Payload
sections.content:
For the flexible file layout type, the body is an ff_layout_wcc4 structure. It holds an array of ff_mirror_wcc4, each with an array of ff_data_server_wcc4. Each data server entry has a device ID, a stateid, an array of filehandles and the attributes (ffdsw_attributes). There MUST be a one-to-one correspondence with ff_layout4, ff_mirror4 and ff_data_server4 from RFC 8435.

Position alone is not enough to say which attributes to update. In a layout with three mirrors where two changed, a client may present all three (one with no attributes) or only the two. Either way, ffdsw_deviceid, ffdsw_stateid and ffdsw_fh_vers together uniquely identify the target, and all three are required, since one storage device may hold several data files. The attributes are processed like those in SETATTR arguments.
sections.eli5: Each note names exactly which shelf, which key and which book it describes, so the librarian never mixes them up.

sections.title: Errors, Optionality and Security
sections.content:
No new errors are introduced. The errors that LAYOUT_WCC can raise are listed in a table, all defined in RFC 8881, including NFS4ERR_BAD_STATEID, NFS4ERR_NOTSUPP and NFS4ERR_UNKNOWN_LAYOUTTYPE. On error the metadata server can ignore the whole operation or apply part of the payload.

The operation is OPTIONAL for both NFSv4.2 and the flexible file layout type. The Security Considerations section says there are no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 8435, and the document has no IANA actions.
sections.eli5: Nobody has to use the notes, and they add no new danger beyond what the system already had.
